after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
$$
[\begin{aligned}a & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & b \\ 0 & 0 & c\end{aligned}]
$$

The matrix of the bilinear form $B(x,y)={x}_{1}{y}_{1}-3{x}_{1}{y}_{3}+{x}_{2}{y}_{3}-{x}_{3}{y}_{3}$ is given above. What is the value of $a+b+c?$
after.worked_solution:
Each term ${a}_{ij}{x}_{i}{y}_{j}$ in the expression of the bilinear form corresponds to the entry ${a}_{ij}$ of the matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}B(x,y) & ={x}_{1}{y}_{1}-3{x}_{1}{y}_{3}+{x}_{2}{y}_{3}-{x}_{3}{y}_{3} \\  & =1{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+0{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+(-3){x}_{1}{y}_{3} \\  & +\,0{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+0{x}_{2}{y}_{2}+1{x}_{2}{y}_{3} \\  & +\,0{x}_{3}{y}_{1}+0{x}_{3}{y}_{2}+(-1){x}_{3}{y}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, the corresponding matrix of the bilinear form is

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, $a=1,$ $b=1,$ and $c=-1.$ Finally, 

$$
a+b+c=1+1+(-1)=1.
$$

after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ above. Which of the following represents the corresponding bilinear form ${x}^{T}\,Ay$ in terms of the components of $x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$ and $y=[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]?$
after.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

Each entry ${a}_{ij}$ of $A$ corresponds to the term ${a}_{ij}{x}_{i}{y}_{j}$ in the expression of the bilinear form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ay & =3{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+1{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+(-1){x}_{2}{y}_{1}+2{x}_{2}{y}_{2} \\  & =3{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+{x}_{1}{y}_{2}-{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+2{x}_{2}{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

To write down a bilinear form in terms of vector components, we compute the following expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ay & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & {x}_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & {x}_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3{y}_{1}+{y}_{2} \\ -{y}_{1}+2{y}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={x}_{1}(3{y}_{1}+{y}_{2})+{x}_{2}(-{y}_{1}+2{y}_{2}) \\  & =3{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+{x}_{1}{y}_{2}-{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+2{x}_{2}{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Writing Down a Bilinear Form Given Its Matrix
content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ above. Which of the following represents the corresponding bilinear form ${x}^{T}\,Ay$ in terms of the components of $x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$ and $y=[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]?$
content.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

Each entry ${a}_{ij}$ of $A$ corresponds to the term ${a}_{ij}{x}_{i}{y}_{j}$ in the expression of the bilinear form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ay & =3{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+1{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+(-1){x}_{2}{y}_{1}+2{x}_{2}{y}_{2} \\  & =3{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+{x}_{1}{y}_{2}-{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+2{x}_{2}{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

To write down a bilinear form in terms of vector components, we compute the following expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ay & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & {x}_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & {x}_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3{y}_{1}+{y}_{2} \\ -{y}_{1}+2{y}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={x}_{1}(3{y}_{1}+{y}_{2})+{x}_{2}(-{y}_{1}+2{y}_{2}) \\  & =3{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+{x}_{1}{y}_{2}-{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+2{x}_{2}{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ -3 & -4\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ above. Which of the following represents the corresponding bilinear form ${x}^{T}\,Ay$ in terms of the components of $x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$ and $y=[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]?$
after.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

Each entry ${a}_{ij}$ of $A$ corresponds to the term ${a}_{ij}{x}_{i}{y}_{j}$ in the expression of the bilinear form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ay & =(3){x}_{1}{y}_{1}+2{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+(-3){x}_{2}{y}_{1}+-4{x}_{2}{y}_{2} \\  & =3{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+2{x}_{1}{y}_{2}-3{x}_{2}{y}_{1}-4{x}_{2}{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

To write down a bilinear form in terms of vector components, we compute the following expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ay & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & {x}_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ -3 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & {x}_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3{y}_{1}+2{y}_{2} \\ -3{y}_{1}-4{y}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={x}_{1}(3{y}_{1}+2{y}_{2})+{x}_{2}(-3{y}_{1}-4{y}_{2}) \\  & =3{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+2{x}_{1}{y}_{2}-3{x}_{2}{y}_{1}-4{x}_{2}{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ -3 & -4\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ above. Which of the following represents the corresponding bilinear form ${x}^{T}\,Ay$ in terms of the components of $x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$ and $y=[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]?$
content.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

Each entry ${a}_{ij}$ of $A$ corresponds to the term ${a}_{ij}{x}_{i}{y}_{j}$ in the expression of the bilinear form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ay & =(3){x}_{1}{y}_{1}+2{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+(-3){x}_{2}{y}_{1}+-4{x}_{2}{y}_{2} \\  & =3{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+2{x}_{1}{y}_{2}-3{x}_{2}{y}_{1}-4{x}_{2}{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

To write down a bilinear form in terms of vector components, we compute the following expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ay & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & {x}_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ -3 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & {x}_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3{y}_{1}+2{y}_{2} \\ -3{y}_{1}-4{y}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={x}_{1}(3{y}_{1}+2{y}_{2})+{x}_{2}(-3{y}_{1}-4{y}_{2}) \\  & =3{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+2{x}_{1}{y}_{2}-3{x}_{2}{y}_{1}-4{x}_{2}{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
Each term ${a}_{ij}{x}_{i}{y}_{j}$ in the expression of the bilinear form corresponds to the entry ${a}_{ij}$ of the matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}B(x,y) & ={x}_{1}{y}_{2}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{1}-3{x}_{3}{y}_{2}+2{x}_{3}{y}_{3} \\  & =0{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+1{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+0{x}_{1}{y}_{3} \\  & +\,3{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+0{x}_{2}{y}_{2}+0{x}_{2}{y}_{3} \\  & +\,0{x}_{3}{y}_{1}+(-3){x}_{3}{y}_{2}+2{x}_{3}{y}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, the corresponding matrix of the bilinear form is

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, $a=1,$ $b=3,$ and $c=2.$ Finally, 

$$
a+b+c=1+3+2=6.
$$
